title: Protocol for the analysis of phenolic compounds using nano-liquid chromatography-mass spectrometry and Caco-2 assays: from the evaluation of the uptake to the enterocyte metabolism
protocol: Pre-column re-equilibration: pump 2.5 μL/min for 2 min with mobile phase A.
Column re-equilibration: pump 0.3 μL/min for 8.3 min with mobile phase A.
Load sample using loading conditions of 2.5 μL/min for 2.4 min with mobile phase A.
Maintain autosampler temperature at 7 °C.
Inject a volume of 5 μl.
Pump flow rate: maintain at 0.3 μL/min.

Apply multi-step linear gradient: from 5% B to 26% B in 0-2 min; from 26% B to 31% B in 2-14.5 min; from 31% B to 36% B in 14.5-21 min; from 36% B to 60% B in 21-23 min; from 60% B to 80% B in 23 to 25 min; maintain at 80% B for 25 to 26 min; then return to 5% B by 28 min.
Maintain initial conditions for an additional 12 min post gradient completion.
Perform MS analysis in negative ionization mode.
Set nebulizing gas pressure to 0.5 bar.
Set drying gas temperature to 150 °C.
Adjust drying gas flow to 5.0 L/min.
Set mass range from m/z 50-1000 for phenolic compounds.
Set capillary voltage to 3.7 KV.
Set end-plate offset to -500 V.
Set capillary exit to -80 V.
Set skimmer 1 to -50 V.
Re-calibrate prior to compound characterization using the lock-mass calibration option.
Dissolve hexakis(2,2-difluoroethoxy)phosphazine at 2 mg/mL in 2-propanol.
Apply the calibrant solution to an adsorber material above 50 μL.
Place the adsorber inside a reservoir mounted on top of the spray shield.
Use the formic aduct as reference mass with an intensity of at least 2,000 counts.
Prepare stock solutions of phenolic compounds in methanol at 1 mg/mL.
Mix HBSS acidified with an aqueous solution of formic acid (10%, v/v) in a proportion of 40:2 (v/v).
Dilute the stock solution from 5 μg/mL to the limit of detection using the dilution solvent.
Obtain at least five calibration points considering the limit of quantification and accuracy values.
Prepare donor and receiver chambers with phenolic compounds dissolved in HBSS.
Add phenolic compounds to the donor chamber and HBSS without compounds to the receiver chamber.
Incubate at 37°C for 0, 30, 60, 90, and 120 minutes.
Take samples from donor and receiver chambers at specified times.
Centrifuge samples for 15 min at 12,000 rpm and 4°C.
Acidify supernatant with formic acid solution in a proportion of 40:2 (v/v).
After transport study, rinse each Caco-2 cell monolayer.
Add 1 mL of HBSS to the cells after rinsing.
Lysate the cells by freezing-thawing three times for 10 min per cycle.
Centrifuge samples at 1,500 rpm for 5 min to obtain supernatant and pellet fractions.
Add ethanol to the solid-particle fraction, centrifuge again, and collect the supernatant.
Treat aliquots of both fractions with methanol in a proportion of 1:5 (v/v).
Vortex-mix treated samples and keep at -20°C for 2 hours.
Centrifuge treated samples at 12,000 rpm for 15 min at 4°C.
Evaporate the solvent from the samples using a vacuum concentrator.
Redissolve dried samples in 40 μL of dilution solvent.
Generate the molecular formula of unknown metabolites using DataAnalysis 4.0 software.
Use SmartFormula™ editor in CHNO algorithm mode.
Compare measured and theoretical masses to identify deviation (Da and ppm).
Evaluate the comparison between theoretical and measured isotope patterns for mSigma value.
Consider rings plus double bonds (rdb) value for molecular formula confidence.
Perform targeted screening using TargetAnalysis™ 1.2 software.
Calibrate with lock-mass calibration method.
Match phenolic compounds based on retention time, accurate m/z, and isotope pattern.
Set retention time error to a narrow range of 0.2 min.
Limit accurate m/z error to a narrow range of <5 ppm.
Apply an mSigma threshold of 75 for isotope pattern matching.
